div.head: IV Atr 2.9
div.ab: Preter discarcatam lanam et dissutum unctum et tres porcos uiuos licebat eis emere in naues suas.
Praeter discarcatam lanam et dissutum unctum, et tres porcos vivos licebat eis emere in naves suas.
Ausser ausgeladener Wolle und zerlassenem Fett durften sie auch drei lebendige Schweine auf ihre Schiffe hin einkaufen.
Besides unloaded wool and rendered fat, they were also allowed to buy three live pigs [to take] onto their ships.
Besides wool, which had been unloaded, and melted fat, they were also permitted to buy three live pigs for their ships.

note.seg: Preter — ui. li. eis überspringt MHkBr
Preter — ui. li. eis omitted by MHkBr

S. Wb: discarcare ‘löschen’. Im Stamforder Marktrecht 1258 muss man lanam decariare et aperire in presencia vicinorum; Bateson Records of Leicester I 79. Höhlbaum Hans. Urkb. III S. 335 vergleicht das Englische Statut 1353: es verbietet dem Kaufmann, den Waren entgegenzureisen behufs Verkaufes, antequam fuerint discarcata. Vgl. Gl Wolle 4. [Er zweifelt, ob nicht laine deffaite (ebd. S. 391) damit identisch; dies erklärt als ‘unwrought’ Riley. T's Lesung discartatam versteht ‘uncarded’ Nicolas ohne Beleg; ‘Karde(n)’ heisst mlat., mfrz., mengl. card (-o, -er), und die Verneinung würde durch in- gebildet sein]

See Wb: discarcare ‘unload’. In the Stamford market law of 1258 one must lanam decariare et aperire in presencia vicinorum; Bateson Records of Leicester I 79. Höhlbaum Hans. Urkb. III p. 335 compares the English statute of 1353: it forbids the merchant to travel out to meet goods for the purpose of sale antequam fuerint discarcata. Cf. Gl Wolle 4. [He wonders whether laine deffaite (ibid. p. 391) is not identical with it; Riley explains this as ‘unwrought’. Nicolas, without evidence, understands T's reading discartatam as ‘uncarded’; ‘card(s)’ is card (-o, -er) in Med. Latin, Middle French and Middle English, and the negative would be formed with in-]

ungere, unguentum sind das Lemma für Agsächs. Glossen smirwan, smeoru. Butter neben einem Schwein darf der Fremde nach Apenrader Skra einkaufen; Steenstrup Danelag 379. [Also unnötig zieht vins descosuz heran Höhlbaum III 391.] Vgl. Gl Fett 2. a

ungere, unguentum are the lemmata for the Anglo-Saxon glosses smirwan, smeoru. Under the Apenrade Skra the foreigner may buy butter alongside a pig; Steenstrup Danelag 379. [So Höhlbaum III 391 needlessly adduces vins descosuz.] Cf. Gl Fett 2. a
Ebenso der Lothringer in London im 12. Jh.; Höhlbaum ebd.
Likewise the Lotharingian in London in the 12th cent.; Höhlbaum ibid.
i.e. wool which is for sale by retail.
unctum, i.e. unguentum, A.S. smeoru, as Liebermann points out.
Presumably as provision, cf. the twelfth-century regulations quoted above, § 10: ‘No Lorrainer may buy more than three live pigs for his table.’
